quarterly_data.quarter: SpaceX Goldman Sachs Communacopia + Technology Conference 2026 (09-10-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: NEW HOSTING DEAL SIGNED AFTER THE Q2 CALL - ANOTHER ~$13 BILLION OF ARR FROM DECEMBER 1: CFO Bret Johnsen gave a post-earnings update: 'just earlier this month, we closed another hosting deal, and that translates into about $1.11 billion a month starting December 1st of this year, which is another roughly $13 billion of ARR that starts December 1st of this year. I would say we have even more conviction now about that $100 billion ARR target by the end of this year.' He also disclosed the structure of the compute deals for the first time: 'Almost all of them, if not all of them, have been, in essence, 90-day with a 90-day out, so roughly six-month commits', including the new one, because SpaceX does not want to give away compute its own Grok products will need.
quarterly_data.figure: new hosting deal ~$1.11 billion a month from December 1st, roughly $13 billion of ARR; $100 billion ARR target reaffirmed; compute deals structured 90-day with a 90-day out (roughly six-month commits)

quarterly_data.quarter: SpaceX Goldman Sachs Communacopia + Technology Conference 2026 (09-10-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: 5-10 GIGAWATTS DEPLOYED NEXT YEAR, WITH POWER - NOT GPUs - AS THE GATING ITEM: Johnsen said 'We talked about a range next year of 5-10 gigawatts deployed... Ending this year with a little over 2', and that the confidence comes from vertical integration and having 'line of sight to the power specifically' - 'because some of it we're going to stand up ourselves' 'in existing locations.' He added: 'We wouldn't give that range for next year unless we had line of sight to power specifically, but power and facilities and permitting needed', and said the industry is now confirming Musk's earlier call that power, not the rest of the supply chain, becomes the constraint.
quarterly_data.figure: 5-10 gigawatts deployed next year versus a little over 2 gigawatts exiting this year

quarterly_data.quarter: SpaceX Goldman Sachs Communacopia + Technology Conference 2026 (09-10-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: ORBITAL COMPUTE MOVES INTO THE NEAR TERM - FIRST SATELLITES FLY NEXT YEAR, SCALE FROM 2028: Johnsen said 'We're actually targeting to fly our first orbital compute satellites next year', with 'huge amounts of compute into space going into 2028.' The hardware is 'largely the same V3 bus' now flying for Starlink broadband, with the payload swapped out and larger solar arrays, so Starship cadence carries it. He argued the cost crossover comes from reusability - terrestrial cost (power, cooling, construction, real estate) is inflating while orbital rides the rocket and satellite cost curve down - and that parity could arrive 'maybe as soon as next year', once both Starship stages are reflown.
quarterly_data.figure: first orbital compute satellites targeted to fly next year; large-scale orbital compute going into 2028

quarterly_data.quarter: SpaceX Goldman Sachs Communacopia + Technology Conference 2026 (09-10-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: GPU ALLOCATION IS THE ONE PIECE SPACEX DOES NOT CONTROL: Johnsen on the NVIDIA relationship - 'we came out and talked about the fact that we're NVIDIA exclusive. That strong relationship, we hope certainly will translate into good allocation from a compute perspective because that's the piece that we don't control.' He argued SpaceX earns allocation by actually standing the compute up, 'not maybe not just for themselves, but also for the industry.' On residual value he said 'you are seeing the monetization of many generations old now compute from NVIDIA still holding its own from a pricing perspective', which is creating 'a whole asset class related to GPU financing.'
